feature: Cutting a stretch out takes the captions along
summary: Deleting a piece of a recording now takes the same stretch out of the whole timeline: captions for the words that went are gone, captions, titles and sounds after the cut move up with the picture, and a caption across the join is shortened. One undo puts it all back.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a screen recording with somebody talking and wait for the captions to write themselves.
Put the playhead in the middle and press Command K, then at a quarter and press Command K again.
Press Delete to throw the middle piece away.
Look at the Captions track: it now ends where V1 ends, with no lines left for the words you cut.
Drop a second clip on the end of V1 and play across the join.

evaluate: After the delete, does every caption still sit over the words it says?
Is it right that the caption across the join keeps its whole line of text, just for less time?
Is it right that a separate sound running under the whole cut (music, a detached voiceover) stays where it was?
Do you ever want Delete on a piece to leave the rest of the timeline alone, the way Premiere's plain Delete does?
rough: A caption across the join keeps all of its words on screen, including any that were said inside the stretch you cut; only its time is shortened, the way Premiere trims a caption clip.

A sound running across the whole cut is left as it was, as the cut mock says for a detached voiceover. If that sound is speech, it is now out of step with the picture after the join, and nothing on the timeline says so.
Nothing on screen says which tracks a delete moved. The cut mock asks this as an open question; there is no per-track sync lock yet.
Delete and Ripple Delete on a piece of a clip now do the same thing. They still differ on a whole clip: Delete leaves a gap, Ripple Delete closes it.
